asparagus-frozen-cooked-fat-added-ns-as-.title: Asparagus, frozen, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus (Asparagus officinalis) is a tender spring vegetable. Frozen cooked asparagus with added fat is typically blanched, then flash‑frozen. Fat (usually a vegetable oil) is added to enhance flavor and mouthfeel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the first vegetables to appear after winter.
In ancient Rome it was a luxury food, symbolizing wealth.
There are three main varieties: green, white (grown in darkness), and purple.
Freezing preserves most vitamins, especially vitamin C and folate.
Adding fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Asparagus provides folate (vitamin B9), essential for DNA synthesis and healthy pregnancy.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100 g serving of frozen cooked asparagus with fat contains about 70 kcal, making it diet‑friendly.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Contains glutathione and vitamin C, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Fiber and potassium aid normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Sodium in processed product
items.content: Industrial processing may add salt; people with hypertension should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen cooked asparagus with added fat can be reheated in a skillet, microwave, or added to soups, stews, and salads. Serve as a side dish, optionally drizzled with a squeeze of lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.

double-hamburger-on-wheat-bun-2-small-pa.title: Double hamburger on wheat bun, 2 small patties

content.title: About
content.content: The double hamburger consists of a wheat bun, two small beef patties (about 50 g each), lettuce, a slice of tomato, pickles, onion and sauce. It is a classic fast‑food item popular in quick‑service restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The wheat bun provides a soft texture and a subtle sweetness, making it an ideal base for a double burger.
Two small patties allow better control of fat content while preserving a rich meat flavor.
The traditional American double burger is often served with cheese, but the basic version can be cheese‑free.
Fresh vegetables and sauce create a balanced flavor profile with acidity and crunch.
The burger is commonly served with fries and a soft drink as a complete meal.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The patties provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is a source of vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef offers heme iron, which is readily absorbed and helps transport oxygen in the blood.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Lettuce, tomato and pickles add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low carbohydrate patties
items.content: Because the patties are small, the overall carbohydrate load remains low, fitting low‑carb diets.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Beef patties contain saturated fats, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Sauces and pickles often add sodium and sugar, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A double burger is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Meat contamination
items.content: Undercooked patties may harbor pathogenic bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the burger hot, split the bun, and layer the patties, vegetables and sauce. It is typically eaten with hands, though a fork and knife can be used if the bun is very soft.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared burgers are best eaten immediately. If you need to store them, let them cool to room temperature, place in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Reheat in an oven or microwave before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate ice cream soda is a carbonated dessert drink that blends the creamy taste of ice cream with a sweet chocolate note and a refreshing fizz. It is often served in a glass with a scoop of ice cream and may include chocolate candy pieces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first carbonated ice cream recipes appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
The chocolate flavor makes the drink popular with both children and adults.
The soda base gives a light foam and a characteristic "tingling" sensation.
In some countries the drink is served with whipped cream and a dusting of cocoa powder.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The soda delivers fast‑acting carbohydrates for rapid energy replenishment.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains dairy ingredients, which may cause discomfort for those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Chocolate allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the ice cream soda chilled, immediately after preparation to retain carbonation. You can top it with whipped cream, sprinkle grated chocolate, or garnish with a cherry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared drink in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours to maintain fizz. Longer storage will cause the carbonation to dissipate and the texture to change.
